'''''Ipomoea carnea''''', the '''pink morning glory''', is a species of [[morning glory]] that grows as a bush. This flowering plant has heart-shaped leaves that are a rich green and {{convert|6|–|9|in|cm}} long. It can be easily grown from seeds. These seeds are toxic and it can be hazardous to cattle; the toxicity is related to the [[swainsonine]] produced by its endophytes,<ref>{{cite journal | pmid = 27436221 | doi=10.1021/acs.jafc.6b02390 | volume=64 | issue=31 | title=Analysis of Swainsonine and Swainsonine N-Oxide as Trimethylsilyl Derivatives by Liquid Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry and Their Relative Occurrence in Plants Toxic to Livestock | year=2016 | journal=J Agric Food Chem | pages=6156–62  | last1 = Gardner | first1 = DR | last2 = Cook | first2 = D}}</ref> and to [[bioaccumulation]] of [[selenium]] in the leaves but mostly in the seeds.<ref name="Sabogal">{{cite journal|last=Sabogal|first=Ana|author2= Dunin Borkowski |date=December 2007|title=[Estado actual de la investigación sobre Ipomoea carnea: toxicidad en ganado caprino] |journal=Revista de Química |publisher=Pontificia Universidad Católica del Perú|location=Lima, Perú|issue=January–December 2007|pages=29–35|issn=1012-3946 }}</ref> Ingestion of seeds or leaves causes abnormal endocrine functions and gastrointestinal functions, immune system alternation, abnormality in embryogenesis.<ref name="FH">{{Cite journal | last= Abid Aqsa, Mushtaq Ahmad, Muhammad Zafar, Sadia Zafar, Mohamed Fawzy Ramadan, Ashwaq T. Althobaiti, Shazia Sultana, Omer Kilic, Trobjon Makhkamov, Akramjon Yuldashev, Oybek Mamarakhimov, Khislat Khaydarov, Afat O. Mammadova, Komiljon Komilov |first= and Salman Majeed |date=December 2023|title= Foliar epidermal and trichome micromorphological diversity among poisonous plants and their taxonomic significance|journal=[[Folia Horticulturae]]|language=en|volume=35|issue=2|pages=243–274|doi= 10.2478/fhort-2023-0019 |issn=2083-5965|doi-access=free}}</ref>

The stem of ''I. carnea'' can be used for making paper.<ref name="Chand">{{cite journal|last=Chand|first=Navin|author2=P. K. Rohatgi|date=June 20, 2005|title=Impact toughness of Ipomoea carnea particulate-polyester composite |journal=Journal of Materials Science Letters |publisher=Springer Netherlands|location=Netherlands|volume=6|issue=6|pages=695–697|issn=0261-8028|doi=10.1007/bf01770929}}</ref> The plant is also of medicinal value.<ref name="Chand" />  It contains a component identical to marsilin, a sedative and anticonvulsant.<ref name="Chand" />  A glycosidic saponin has also been purified from ''I. carnea'' with anticarcinogenic and oxytocic properties.<ref name="Chand" />

One selection of ''I. carnea'', 'Inducer', has been used as a [[rootstock]] for inducing flowering of [[sweetpotato]] cultivars which otherwise prove reticent to produce flowers.<ref name="Dukes">{{cite journal|last=Dukes|first=P.D.|author2=A. Jones|author3=J.M. Schalk|date=1990|title='Inducer', a tree morning glory rootstock cultivar for use in breeding sweetpotatoes. |journal=HortScience |volume=25|issue=2|pages=238–239|issn=0018-5345|doi=10.21273/hortsci.25.2.238|doi-access=free}}</ref>

Another common name is "bush morning glory", but particularly in temperate [[North America]], that usually refers to ''[[Ipomoea leptophylla|I. leptophylla]]''.
[[File:Ipomoea carnea July 2025.jpg|thumb|Ipomoea carnea leaves ]]
In [[Brazil]], ''I. carnea'' (in addition to other common names) is known as ''canudo-de-pito'', literally "pipe-cane", as its hollow stems were used to make tubes for [[tobacco pipe]]s. It thus became the namesake of [[Canudos]], a religious community in the [[sertão]] of [[Bahia]], over which the [[War of Canudos]] was fought 1893–1897.
